candidates.title: Directed soft-assignment geometry with global codeword repulsion
candidates.falsifier: Reject if source-target exchange does not change the loss, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite on the checker case, or the cold run increases level-0 Gini, reduces L1-to-L2 branches, increases train-to-test frequency drift, lowers sequence information, or fails to improve Stage-3 recall@10 against control.
candidates.risk: The global repulsion may distort useful codebook geometry or be too weak to counter codeword convergence induced by the host objective. Its directed distance term may improve pair fit by changing assignments in a way that still increases level-0 usage concentration or harms downstream ranking; the frozen downstream evaluation is needed to detect that.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The directed distance term updates codewords according to source-weighted target residuals. The repulsion term pushes every codeword pair apart, independently of transition pairing. It contains no attractive source-target codeword term, so it cannot pull a transition's two codewords together; repulsion opposes such convergence.

candidates.title: Directed soft transition objective preserving assignment branches
candidates.falsifier: Reject if source-target exchange leaves the loss unchanged, declared gradients are zero or non-finite, or the exported codes violate any measured structural requirement or fail to improve Stage-3 recall@10 against control.
candidates.risk: Conditional entropy can increase by spreading soft assignments without improving hard assignments, or can favor noisy branches that do not help recommendation. The target-fit component may still concentrate marginal code usage, and the entropy reward may trade pair-level ER against useful sequence structure.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The source-conditioned target-fit term updates codewords toward targets weighted by source assignment. The conditional-entropy term differentiates through both endpoint assignments and rewards multiple target branches for a given source code. It does not contain an attraction between the two endpoint codewords; branch entropy instead penalizes collapsing all target assignments to one branch, though it does not by itself guarantee balanced marginal code usage.

candidates.title: Source-conditioned residual transport with codeword separation
candidates.falsifier: Reject if source-target exchange leaves the loss unchanged, any declared gradient is zero or non-finite, or the exported codes fail any structural requirement or do not improve Stage-3 recall@10 against control.
candidates.risk: The residual and separation terms can oppose each other or move codewords away from useful target regions, degrading quantization or increasing frequency drift. Separation may raise pair-level ER without preserving marginal balance, prefix width, sequence information, or downstream recommendation quality.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The residual term moves the source-weighted codebook centroid relative to the target; the separation reward pushes source-selected codewords away from the target. This is not an attractive force between the source and target codewords, so it does not directly pull a transition's two codewords together. Its codebook gradients can nevertheless distort other codeword relationships.
